scope_note: Blender 5.2 LTS manual and one FlightGear c172p open-source issue are the verified basis. No Blender or engine run. Engine-specific vehicle APIs are not asserted.

sources.title: Bone Structure
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Main text on bone head/tail, roll, and local axes.
supports: A bone has head, body, and tail; its local Y axis is aligned from root to tip and is the roll axis.
Bone local axes are not world axes.
limits: Does not define any engine skeleton convention.
Read as extracted manual text, not executed.

independent_primary_check.root_review: body sections read by independent reviewer; D03/D10 also read by root

sources.title: Bone Roll
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Bone roll definition and recalculate/set/clear roll operations.
supports: Roll is the rest-pose rotation around the bone length.
Roll can be recalculated against local/global/view/cursor references or cleared.
limits: Does not prescribe a roll convention for wheels, hinges, or engines.

independent_primary_check.root_review: body sections read by independent reviewer; D03/D10 also read by root

sources.title: Skinning Introduction
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Main text distinguishing object/bone parenting from Armature modifier deformation.
supports: Objects parented or constrained to bones are transformed but never deformed.
The Armature modifier is the path that modifies vertex/control-point relative positions.
limits: Conceptual distinction; no vehicle-specific workflow or engine behavior.

sources.title: Armature Modifier
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Armature modifier purpose, Vertex Groups/Envelopes, Multi Modifier, empty-group tip.
supports: Bones deform vertices in same-named vertex groups when Vertex Groups binding is used.
The modifier deforms existing geometry; multiple armature modifiers can be mixed via Multi Modifier.
limits: Does not state a universal influence count or guarantee auto weights.
No engine skinning contract.

sources.title: Armature Deform Parent
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Armature Deform parenting, Empty/Automatic/Envelope weights, Cube+BoneA/B/C example, overwrite warning.
supports: Armature Deform parenting makes the armature the parent and adds an Armature modifier to each child.
Empty Groups creates empty groups named after deform bones; automatic weights may need manual correction.
Automatic/envelope weights overwrite existing same-named vertex group content.
limits: Not a vehicle example; no wheel radius, suspension, mass, collision, or engine import.
Parent+modifier is the documented setup, not evidence about engine double transforms.

sources.title: Weight Paint Introduction
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Weight paint purpose, normalized weights, armature auto-normalization, locking and multi-paint.
supports: Deformation weights usually need normalization; the Armature modifier normalizes automatically.
Normalized workflow and locking help control redistribution.
limits: Does not state a four-influence cap; engine limits must be verified separately.

sources.title: Parenting Objects
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Object parent, Keep Transform, Parent Inverse, Clear Parent, non-uniform scale limitation.
supports: Object parent transforms children but children do not transform the parent.
Keep Transform computes Parent Inverse to preserve world transform.
A rotated parent with non-uniform scale can shear a child; clearing parent may lose the shear.
limits: Does not define engine parent/attachment behavior.

sources.title: Apply (Object)
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Apply Location/Rotation/Scale/Rotation & Scale, shared data warning, armature caveat.
supports: Applying transforms resets object values and changes how modifiers/constraints/parenting evaluate.
Applying to armatures does not affect pose transforms, animation curves, or constraints; apply before rigging is recommended.
limits: Does not require applying every object or every transform.

sources.title: Inverse Kinematics Constraint
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: IK purpose, pole target, iterations, chain length, stretch, position/rotation weights, evaluation order.
supports: IK rotates a chain to follow a target; pole target determines chain roll/elbow direction.
Chain length, iterations, stretch, and weights are explicit settings.
IK constraints modify multiple bones and are evaluated after other constraints on affected bones.
limits: Does not guarantee arbitrary closed-loop mechanisms.
No engine IK contract.

sources.title: Inverse Kinematics Introduction
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: IK solver overview, iTaSC, precision/iterations, reiteration, substeps, stability and arm example.
supports: IK stability depends on precision, iterations, and substeps; unstable motion can be improved with more steps.
Substep duration guidance is about 10 ms in the manual's example.
limits: No universal iteration/substep values for vehicles or mechs.

sources.title: Spline IK Constraint
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Spline IK purpose, chain length/fitting, even divisions, chain offset, scale modes, setup guidance.
supports: Spline IK fits a bone chain to a curve and is suited to flexible parts and ropes.
Bone length/rest shape and chain scaling modes affect the fit.
limits: No direct vehicle track/hose example; requires testing.

sources.title: Rigid Body Introduction
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Rigid body scope, active/passive, animation interaction, transform behavior, scale, mesh-only constraint.
supports: Rigid body simulation moves/orients objects but does not deform them.
Only mesh objects can be rigid bodies.
Active bodies are simulated; passive bodies are animated; simulation overrides dynamic transforms.
limits: Blender-specific; does not describe engine vehicle physics.

sources.title: Rigid Body Collisions
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Collision shapes, primitive vs mesh/convex, compound parent, source base/deform/final, deforming, surface response, margin, collections.
supports: Primitive shapes are fastest; convex hull/mesh better approximate geometry; compound parent combines child shapes for concave proxies.
Collision source can be base, deformed, or final mesh; deformation can be enabled.
Mesh/convex shapes use object origin as center of gravity; primitives use geometric center.
limits: Does not provide vehicle-specific collider dimensions or mass values.

sources.title: Rigid Body Constraints Introduction
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Constraint host/anchor behavior, breakable/threshold, disable collisions, limits, iterations, Child Of alternative.
supports: Rigid body constraints usually attach to an Empty; anchor points are fixed in each object's local space at simulation start.
Breakable allows a constraint to break at an impulse threshold; disable collisions lets constrained objects pass through each other.
Motor constraints are not breakable.
limits: Does not define engine constraint export or runtime destruction.

sources.title: Motor Constraint
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Motor translation/rotation, axis semantics, Hinge comparison, alignment warning, target velocity/max impulse.
supports: Motor rotation uses the constraint host's X axis; Hinge uses Z.
If the axes are not aligned, the motor may appear to have no effect because the hinge blocks motion.
limits: Blender rigid-body mechanism only; not an engine wheel-motor contract.

sources.title: Rigid Body Tips
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Baking to keyframes, steps per second, solver iterations, small objects, mesh-shape tunneling, collision thickness.
supports: Rigid body dynamics can be baked to normal keyframes.
Small objects are less stable; the manual suggests about 20 cm as a practical guideline.
Thin mesh shapes can tunnel; more steps/iterations can improve stability but excessive steps are not a cure-all.
limits: The 20 cm figure is a guideline, not a universal hard gate.

sources.title: glTF 2.0
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Supported features, animation import/export modes, action/NLA requirements, only transform/pose-bone/shape-key animation, sampling, armature export options.
supports: glTF animation changes object transforms, pose bones, or shape-key values.
Physics, light, and material property animation are ignored by the supported animation subset.
Actions must be active or stashed to NLA; sampling is recommended when exporting constrained animation.
Armature export offers rest-position and deform-bones-only options.
limits: Does not define engine import behavior beyond glTF.
glTF adaptation may lose Blender-specific constraints/controllers.

sources.title: FBX (Legacy)
sources.author: Blender Foundation / Blender Manual contributors
sources.read_scope: Bake animation, constraints missing, bone orientation correction, armature instances unsupported, action linking notes.
supports: FBX exports constraint results as keyframes but does not save the constraints themselves.
Bone orientation may need correction because FBX/Blender bone axes differ.
Armature instances are not supported.
limits: FBX-specific; not a general rigging correctness statement.

sources.title: glTF 2.0 Skin schema
sources.author: Khronos Group
sources.version_date: glTF 2.0 schema on main; no commit pinned; read 2026-11-13
sources.read_scope: Raw skin schema: joints, inverseBindMatrices, skeleton root requirements.
supports: A glTF skin's joints are node indices; inverseBindMatrices is an accessor with at least one matrix per joint; skeleton is a node index.
Skeletal consumption is structural (node/joint indices), not a required business-name convention.
limits: Schema only; does not assert per-vertex influence count, engine limits, or Blender exporter behavior.
Main-branch snapshot was not pinned to a commit.

sources.title: Howto: Animate models
sources.author: FlightGear Wiki contributors
sources.version_date: FlightGear Wiki; no reliable page date exposed; read 2026-11-13
sources.read_scope: Relevant sections: object-name, property, animation order, axis, center, rotate, factor/offset, geometry axis/center since 2017.2.
supports: A part must be named in the 3D model and matched by object-name; animations without object-name apply to the entire model.
Rotate animations use a property, axis, center, factor, and offset; animation order matters.
A geometry object can define axis/center for some animations since 2017.2.
limits: FlightGear-specific XML format; not Blender or general engine behavior.
Page appears maintained but no reliable version date was exposed.

sources.title: c172p PR #992: Add elevator trim tab
sources.author: c172p-team; PR author wlbragg; comments by gilbertohasnofb, dany93, et al.
sources.read_scope: PR title/body and selected review comments about trim-tab animation axis, target object, proportionality, and direction.

Reviewers called for a rotation-axis adjustment and proportional trim-tab motion.
The trim tab's direction relative to the elevator is a concrete sign-convention trap.
limits: Did not read the c172p XML/model files or run FlightGear.
Historical PR, not current FlightGear behavior or a full aircraft rig.
No mass, collision, or flight-dynamics validation.

Visual Transform to Pose bakes evaluated constraint results into regular pose transforms.
